user_query: Why are the learned structural features said to be especially useful with simple machine learning algorithms, even though they can be used with any classifier?
llm_response: The learned structural features are especially useful with simple machine learning algorithms because they turn complex, high-dimensional structure into a compact, informative representation that is easier for a basic classifier to separate. In other words, the feature learning does much of the hard work, so even a simple model like logistic regression, a linear SVM, or a shallow tree can perform well. They can still be used with any classifier, but they are particularly valuable when you want to avoid relying on a very complex model to discover the structure on its own.
llm_confidence_reasoning: This is a general machine-learning principle and the explanation is consistent with how learned representations are typically used, though the exact wording may depend on the source context.
